Kenya’s GDP growth is projected at 5.2 percent in 2026, supported by infrastructure development, agriculture,
SMEs, manufacturing and public sector reforms. Against this backdrop, the Board has set clear priorities
for 2026 and beyond, among them capturing increased credit demand in a lower interest rate environment;
maintaining asset quality; targeting NPLs below 9 percent and improving operational efficiency towards a 40
percent cost toincome ratio. The Group also plans to expand infrastructure financing, enhance its sovereign
advisory capabilities and grow SME and agriculture lending. We will also prioritise the deepening of our wealth
management and affluent banking offerings; leveraging regional trade integration through PAPSS and the AfCFTA
and continue embedding sustainability into our lending and procurement decisions.
